promptAsSent:
Use the image_gen tool to generate exactly one image, then stop. Do not write files, run commands or edit anything.

Attached reference images, in order:
Image 1: Geometry/layout authority: the edit target
Image 2: Material/style only; not layout

Asset type: production-source master for a top-down game sprite: the chassis of the HOUND, a fast, light close-assault walking machine, redesigned as old, low-tech Hegemony armour.

Image 1 is the exact silhouette and layout authority, a grey blockout: fill it in, never move, resize, widen or add to its shapes, and keep all empty canvas empty. From front to back: two narrow cheek plates at the nose with an open channel between them; a slim armoured spine box; a lighter flat rectangular deck down the middle of the spine; two round hip housings at the waist on either side of the deck; two broad armoured skirts angled over the legs on each flank; a squat engine block at the very rear with exhaust grilles. Everything is symmetric about the vertical centre line. Make each shape read as real plate: chamfered edges, rivet rows, weld seams, inspection hatches, grab handles, pipes running along the spine between the skirts.

Image 2 is material and style reference only, never layout: the Hegemony medium tank this walker serves beside. Match its finish exactly: warm tan and khaki cast and welded plate with olive-green panels, heavy rivet rows, exposed piping and cable runs in the seams, worn bright edges, chips, grime and dust, a few orange hazard panels on leading corners, dark gunmetal working parts, crisp painted game-sprite finish, light from the upper left. It is old, low-tech, depot-built Hegemony military hardware: blunt, boxy, bolted and repairable, never sleek, smooth or high-tech.

Strict 90-degree zenith orthographic top-down view of the chassis's top surfaces, the machine facing the TOP edge of the canvas. True transparent background, including all negative space and the open gun channel at the nose; no ground, shadow slab, cast shadow, halo, glow, border, text, labels or logos.

Draw only the chassis body. Do not draw weapons, missile racks, legs, feet or thigh linkages: those are separate layers drawn later. The open channel between the two nose cheek plates must stay empty and transparent, because the gun's barrel shows through it. The flat rectangular deck is where a missile rack is bolted on later: keep it a plain, flat, riveted mounting plate with bolt points, nothing standing on it. The two round housings at the waist are the hip joints the leg linkages leave from: draw them as heavy round bearing housings.

Avoid: sci-fi smooth plastic, glowing lights, blue or cyan, white paint, perspective, side view, isometric view, cropped edges, a second machine, text.
agentMessages: I’ll generate one chassis image using Image 1’s exact geometry and Image 2’s armour finish, with transparent negative space.
